import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_2/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_2/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_2/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_2/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_2/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_2/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_2/training_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_2/training_8.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_2/training_9.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_2/training_10.csv"
]

# Read all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = [pd.read_csv(f, index_col=0) for f in source_files]

# Union all source tables by concatenation
union_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Ensure the column '0' is integer type as per target schema
union_df['0'] = union_df['0'].astype(int)

# Write the result to the target CSV file
union_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_2/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
